critical_questions: What were the specific selection criteria used by CAF, and did they adequately account for Nigerian players' recent performances?
Why does Leadership frame this as a 'snub' rather than examining which players were selected and on what merit?
Are there documented reasons from CAF explaining the exclusion, or is this article presenting incomplete information?

articles.title: Nigeria Targets Chinese Investments In Manufacturing, Agriculture, Mining
articles.summary: Nigeria is seeking to attract increased Chinese investments in manufacturing, agriculture, mining and other critical sectors of its economy as the Federal Government intensifies efforts to deepen bilateral trade and industrial cooperation between both countries. The investment drive took centre stage at the third edition of the Business and Investment Forum organised by the Nigerian […]
articles.hausa_translation: Nijeriya tana neman Kasua Jiya daga Caina a gida-gida, aikin jari, aiki-aiki da wasu mahimman abokan kasuwa. Gwamnatin Tarayya tana kara ƙoƙarin hada gida da kasuwar Caina don ƙara kasua da aiki tare.
critical_questions: What specific terms and equity shares are being negotiated—who truly benefits from these deals?
Why is Nigeria pursuing Chinese investment now, and what domestic manufacturing capacity already exists that could be leveraged instead?
Whose voices are missing: what do Nigerian workers, local small businesses, and environmental groups say about these investment terms?
What happened in previous Chinese investment projects in Nigeria—were promised jobs and technology transfer actually delivered?
How does this framing of 'deepening cooperation' obscure potential debt-dependency or resource extraction dynamics?

articles.title: PDP NWC Meets 37 State Chairmen In Abuja Ahead Of 2027 Elections

The meeting is holding at the party’s national secretariat, Wadata Plaza, under the leadership of the National […]
articles.hausa_translation: Kwamitin Aiki na Tsarin Kasar (NWC) na Jam'iyyar Masu Ci Gaba (PDP) jiya ne suke taron da shugabannin jam'iyyar daga jihohe 36 da Kasuwar Abuuja (FCT) a Abuja kafin zabukan 2027. Taron ya kasance a ofishin jam'iyyar na tsarin kasar, Wadata Plaza, karkashin jagoran Kwamitin Aiki na Tsarin Kasar.
critical_questions: What specific agenda items are being discussed and why is the timing just 2 years before the 2027 election strategically significant?
Which power brokers within the PDP are driving this meeting and whose interests does it serve given recent party factional tensions?
Are state chairmen meeting as equals or is this a top-down directive, and what happens to those who disagree with the central leadership?
What are the implicit expectations regarding candidate selection, funding contributions, or political alignment being set at this meeting?
Why does the incomplete article summary lack details on outcomes, decisions made, or statements from attendees?

articles.title: What is Nigeria’s degree worth in the labour market?

articles.hausa_translation: Digirin Nigeria a kasuwa aikin yadda yake da daraja?

Who benefits from promoting higher education when skill gaps and curriculum misalignment with market demands go unaddressed?
Are universities or employers responsible for graduates' unemployment - and why doesn't the headline explore this structural tension?
What alternative pathways (vocational, apprenticeships) exist, and why are they marginalized in Nigerian education discourse?
Is this World Bank metric useful if it doesn't distinguish between degree quality, field of study, and actual labour market outcomes?

articles.title: Male providers are more involved in shared caregiving – Report

articles.hausa_translation: Masu aikin jiya suna da sannu sosai a cikin kulawa tare - Raport. Maza na Nigeria na jiya suna ganin jiyansa ba kawai a matsayin mai ba da kudin gida ba, amma a matsayin mutum da zafi da bukatarsu a riko daga bakin'ama.
critical_questions: What specific data metrics and sample sizes underpin this 'report'? Who conducted the research and what are their potential biases?
Does this report distinguish between urban elite professionals versus rural or working-class Nigerian men, potentially masking class-based disparities?
Who benefits from this narrative of changing male roles - is this driven by women's rights advocacy, corporate interests in dual-income households, or demographic concerns?
Are women's actual workload and time allocation studied alongside this claim, or does the framing center male participation while obscuring persistent gender care gaps?
What is the publication date and timing context - does this align with policy discussions, corporate campaigns, or international development agendas?

articles.title: Americans Vote In Midterm Elections To Upend Trump Presidency
articles.summary:
Trump returned to office last year promising to bring down prices, but inflation, tariffs and fuel costs inflated by the Middle East conflict have squeezed Americans.
The post Americans Vote In Midterm Elections To Upend Trump Presidency appeared first on Channels Television.
articles.hausa_translation: Amerikanci suna jefa kuri'a a zaben gida don bugi mulkin Trump. Trump ya koma gida jiya da alkawari na rage farashin kayayyaki, amma hauhawar farashin kudin ajiya, tara kwamanda da farashin mai da aka ƙara saboda rikici a gabas ta damje Amerikanci.
critical_questions: This article references 'midterm elections' but Trump's term began recently - are these actually midterm elections or is the timeline being misrepresented?

The summary conflates multiple causes (inflation, tariffs, Middle East fuel costs) without clarifying which policies Trump actually implemented versus inherited conditions - what is the evidence attribution?
Who owns Channels Television and what is their editorial stance on Trump - could ownership bias be shaping the framing?
The headline frames voting as intent to 'upend' Trump's presidency - is this reporting election news or advocating for an outcome?
What specific economic data supports the claim that these factors have 'squeezed Americans' and how does this compare to previous administrations?

articles.title: PDP Petitions IGP Over Alleged Harassment, Killing Of Members In Ebonyi
articles.summary:
Chairman of the PDP state chairmen forum, Austin Nwachukwu, disclosed this at a meeting with the national working committee in Abuja, on Tuesday.

articles.hausa_translation: Shugaban PDP na jihohi, Austin Nwachukwu, ya bayyana cewa PDP ta gabatar da kara'ar gaida ga IGP game da zagi da kisan membocinsu a Ebonyi. Ya faita wannan a wata taron kwamitin jiya a Abuja.
critical_questions: What specific evidence of killings and harassment is the PDP presenting, or are these allegations unsubstantiated claims?

Who are the alleged victims, when did these incidents occur, and why wasn't this raised earlier?
Is there independent verification from security agencies or human rights organizations, or is this a one-sided political narrative?

Are there any known connections between this case and larger organized crime networks, or is this framed solely as petty criminal activity?

articles.title: FG begins N50,000 relief payments to vulnerable Nigerians
articles.summary:
The Federal Government has begun disbursing N50,000 cash relief to vulnerable Nigerians to cushion the effects of the high cost of living under its NERSI.

Read More: https://punchng.com/fg-begins-n50000-relief-payments-to-vulnerable-nigerians/
articles.hausa_translation: Gwamnatin Tarayya ta fara ba da sakamakon kudin N50,000 ga masu rauni a Najeriya domin a rage tasirin tsada kusada a karkashin shirinsanta na NERSI.
critical_questions: What are the specific eligibility criteria for receiving this relief, and how transparent is the selection process to prevent political patronage?
How much of the allocated budget is actually reaching beneficiaries versus being lost to administrative costs and corruption?
Why is N50,000 the chosen amount, and has an impact assessment been conducted to verify if this genuinely addresses cost of living pressures?
What is the timeline and total budget for NERSI, and will this be a one-time payment or sustained relief?
Who are the missing voices - have vulnerable communities been consulted on their actual needs, or is this a top-down measure designed for political optics?

articles.title: Gambia bank sack order threatens jobs of 57 Nigerians – NiDCOM
articles.summary:
NiDCOM has raised concerns that 57 Nigerian professionals in four banks may lose their jobs due to a directive by The Gambia’s central bank.

articles.hausa_translation: Gambia's bank sack order threatens jobs of 57 Nigerians – NiDCOM: NiDCOM ya kaishi damuwa cewa ma'aikatan Naija 57 a bankunan hudu na iya rasa aikinsu saboda umarnin da The Gambia's bank ta ba da shi.
critical_questions: What is the stated rationale from The Gambia's central bank for this directive—is it protectionist policy, regulatory compliance, or something else entirely?

Who benefits from this directive beyond immediate job displacement—which domestic interests or political actors are driving this policy?

What precedent does this set for Nigerian professionals across West Africa, and has there been similar pushback in other countries that should inform this story's framing?

articles.hausa_translation: Gwamnatin Edo ta kashe naira biliyan 14.5 akan tsaron jiya da jiya, amma ba ta ba da kudin gida ga ma'aikacin tsaro. A cikin watan tara, an samu kidnappin da kai da kai a gida duk da kashen kudin.
